habitat: Flocks anywhere, often with other bee-eaters, perching on roadside telephone wires. Flocks often fly at great height.
summary: Newman calls it a common resident and a summer visitor. Turquoise-blue forehead and underparts, a yellow throat, and a gold-and-brown mantle. The colour key also says the upperparts are chestnut and green. The flight call is a clear liquid quilp or kwirry. Because Newman gives both resident and summer visitor, status and months are left unset. The Kemp code NB was left unchanged.
